observations: Photo 0 shows the front/side of a black Xbox console with a power/vent area visible; no power cable/adaptor is shown.
Photo 1 shows a black Xbox controller placed on top of the console; no model label or game discs/cases are visible.
No clear readable branding/model number is visible on the console in these photos.

claims.claim: Xbox one with one pad for sell
claims.evidence: Photos show an Xbox-style console and a controller, but the Xbox One model and that it is exactly 'Xbox One' (vs other Xbox models) are not readable; controller count is only implied by one controller shown.
No game discs, cases, or game titles are shown in either photo.
No adaptor/power brick/cable is shown, and there is no photo of the console powered on or showing a fault.

risks.risk: Console model may not be Xbox One (could be another Xbox generation), which changes compatibility and resale value.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the console label/serial/model number sticker (back/bottom) and/or the disc drive area, plus a photo of the console boot screen.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic Xbox console with power issue (worst case: not reliably working).

risks.risk: Adaptor/power issue could mean more than just the adaptor (e.g., PSU failure, port damage).
risks.proof: Video clip of the console attempting to power on with a known-good adaptor, showing whether it boots to dashboard.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not working / needs repair until proven otherwise.

risks.risk: Controller condition (drift, broken buttons, faulty triggers) is unknown.
risks.proof: Video clip showing controller connected and working in a game/menu (moving sticks, pressing all buttons), or a photo of controller model/serial plus a quick functional test screenshot.

risks.risk: Games may be missing, not included, or not the claimed titles (including 'fc').
risks.proof: Photos of all 6 game cases/discs laid out with titles visible (front covers) or a screenshot of the installed games list (if digital).

risks.risk: Missing accessories (HDMI cable, power cable, headset, etc.) could reduce value.
risks.proof: Photo of everything included laid out on a surface (console, controller, adaptor/power cable, HDMI, and any other items).
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming only the shown items are included.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the console model/serial label (back or bottom) to confirm it is Xbox One and the exact variant.
Video showing the console powering on using a known-good adaptor (or showing the exact adaptor fault).
Photos of all included games (6 discs/cases) with titles visible.
Photo of the exact adaptor/power brick and the power cable included (and whether it’s missing/defective).
Video of the controller working (button presses + stick movement) after connecting.
response.reason: The photos confirm an Xbox-style console and one controller, but the exact Xbox One model, the adaptor fault, and the included 6 games (including FC) are not verifiable from the images. Without proof, the worst-case pricing depends heavily on whether it powers on and which Xbox model it is.
